items.title: Bob Lovett Interview, 1949-04-01
items.q: I began to listen to the Hot Fives, Jelly Roll Morton, King Oliver, and that sort of thing.

ctx.x: I was a little bit of a jazz musician. I was a little bit of a jazz musician. I was a little bit of a jazz musician.

No, I wasn't good enough then. I was just learning. We had a little group, I remember, in Boston, a few fellows I know, including Dan Gerald, who you know, who I was in prep school with. There was a trumpet player and piano player and Dan Gerald on drums and myself. How does Gerald spell his name? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And we used to play at the trumpet player's house. His name was Ted Fales. And I began to become more under New Orleans influence. I began to listen to the Hot Fives, Jelly Roll Morton, King Oliver, and…

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Any records stand out in your mind? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. You mean that I heard? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Do you recall of that period? Yes, that you'd imitate for example. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Oh, yeah. Some of the...
